item.title: eMudhra says it will exit the SSL/TLS certificate business, 1% of its revenue, after its TLS certificates with private keys of just 3 to 8 bits were compromised (Abhirami G/Reuters)
item.description:
Abhirami G / Reuters:
eMudhra says it will exit the SSL/TLS certificate business, 1% of its revenue, after its TLS certificates with private keys of just 3 to 8 bits were compromised  —  Indian digital trust services provider eMudhra (EMUD.NS) on Thursday said it would voluntarily withdraw from the global SSL/TLS …

Original (direct link): https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/indian-firm-emudhra-exits-global-digital-certificates-business-after-2026-10-22/

item.title: Cloudflare's Matthew Prince says PHP2Shell exploit attempts on its network rose from thousands in the 10 hours before the disclosure to millions afterward (Matthew Prince/@eastdakota)
item.description:
Matthew Prince / @eastdakota:
Cloudflare's Matthew Prince says PHP2Shell exploit attempts on its network rose from thousands in the 10 hours before the disclosure to millions afterward  —  Some stats on #php2shell. In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the @Cloudflare network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it. That jumped to tens of thousands in the 45 minutes post announcement, hundreds of thousands within 2 hours, and millions now.

Original (direct link): https://x.com/eastdakota/status/2113079352682570051

item.title: Ukraine says the abrupt throttling of US-funded Starshield grounded dozens of drones mid-flight, costing one unit $1M+, and halted some strikes for three days (New York Times)
item.description:
New York Times:
Ukraine says the abrupt throttling of US-funded Starshield grounded dozens of drones mid-flight, costing one unit $1M+, and halted some strikes for three days  —  Ukraine says it still doesn't know why the military satellite internet service, a sister to Starlink, was abruptly throttled, leaving troops vulnerable to Russian attacks.

Original (direct link): https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/21/world/europe/starshield-starlink-ukraine.html?unlocked_article_code=1.KVE.bUiV.u_YBlM0MuAAB&smid=nytcore-ios-share

item.title: Xona, which plans to deploy a 258-satellite low-Earth orbit constellation as a commercial alternative to GPS, raised a $250M Series D at a $2.45B valuation (Monica Hunter-Hart/Forbes)
item.description:
Monica Hunter-Hart / Forbes:
Xona, which plans to deploy a 258-satellite low-Earth orbit constellation as a commercial alternative to GPS, raised a $250M Series D at a $2.45B valuation  —  The U.S. government built GPS.  Now Silicon Valley is funding a rival developed by the startup Xona, which just raised $250 million in venture funding.

Original (direct link): https://www.forbes.com/sites/monicahunter-hart/2026/10/22/exclusive-spacex-investor-backs-245-billion-startup-taking-the-starlink-model-to-gps/
